title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of a sheaf-theoretic study of line bundles with connection, on the way to p-curvature and the Cartier operation (next page). Notation: f: X→S, f^{fl} is the induced map of fppf sites, P^c_{X/S} is the fppf sheaf of line bundles with relative connection, and P^{ci}_{X/S} ⊂ P^c is the subsheaf where the connection is integrable.

(2.1) Curvature is a homomorphism P^c → f^{fl}_*(Z^2_{X/S}) ⊂ f^{fl}_*(Ω^2_{X/S}), since the curvature of a rank-one connection is a closed 2-form. Its kernel is P^{ci}, giving 0 → P^{ci} → P^c → f_*Z^2.

(2.2) Smooth case. P^{ci} = R^1 f_*(O^× → Ω^1 → Ω^2 → …), with dlog as the first map. The triangle Ω^{≥1}[-1] → (O^× →dlog Ω^{≥1}) → O^× gives 0 → f_*Z^1 / dlog f_*O^× → P^{ci} → Pic_{X/S} → R^2 f_*(0→Ω^1→Ω^2→…).
- The first term is closed 1-forms modulo logarithmic differentials of units, i.e. the integrable connections on the trivial bundle.
- The last map is the de Rham first Chern class, landing in the Hodge piece F^1 H^2_{dR}. This is the obstruction for a line bundle to admit an integrable connection.
- Non-smooth case: the last term is replaced by the sheafification of S' ↦ R^2 f_{S',cris}(J_{X_{S'}/S'}), where J is the augmentation ideal of the crystalline structure sheaf. This is the crystalline version: P^{ci} is read as crystals of invertible modules, and the exact sequence 1 → 1+J → O^×_cris → O^×_X, with log: 1+J ≅ J on PD ideals, gives a Chern class in H^2_cris(J).

Particular case. Assume Pic^0_{X/S} = B is an abelian scheme with dual A^0 = Alb^0_{X/S}, and the Albanese map X → A^1 = Alb^1 (an A^0-torsor) induces f_*Ω^1_{X/S} ≅ g_*Ω^1_{A^1/S}.
- Sufficient conditions: Ω^1 flat with base-change-compatible formation, plus fibrewise bijectivity of H^0(A^1_s, Ω^1) → H^0(X_s, Ω^1).
- This holds for torsors under abelian schemes and for smooth proper curves.
- Then the identity component of P^{ci}_{X/S} is an extension of B by the vector bundle f_*Ω^1_X ≅ ω_A = Lie(A)^∨ = Lie(B^*)^∨, using B^* ≅ A.
- Grothendieck concludes that this is the universal vector extension E(B) of B = Pic^0: Pic^♮ ≅ E(Pic^0).

Next page: since Hom(B, vector group) = 0 and d kills global 1-forms, one gets P^{c,0} = P^{ci,0}. Then, in characteristic p, p-curvature is introduced.

Purpose: an algebraic, base-change-compatible description of the universal vector extension (and hence first de Rham/crystalline cohomology) via line bundles with integrable connection, feeding into the study of Gauss–Manin, Picard–Fuchs and the Cartier operation.
errors: Sheaf-level statements are only sketched: the passage from fibrewise conditions to identification of sheaves (sheafification, representability of f_*Ω^1 by a vector bundle) needs cohomological flatness, which is only partly stated.

The identification as the *universal* extension is asserted from matching the vector part (ω_A = Lie(B^*)^∨). One must still check that the classifying map Hom(ω_A ↔ Ext^1(B, G_a)) is the identity, not just that the groups match; this is left to '....'.
Notational slips: A^1 vs A' vs A in the chain Lie(A)^∨ ≅ f_*^0(Ω^1_{A/S}) ≅ g^1_*(Ω^1_{A'/S}); 'f^0_*' presumably means the structure map of A^0.

In characteristic p the hypothesis that Albanese pulls back 1-forms bijectively can fail beyond curves and abelian torsors (non-reduced Pic). Grothendieck correctly makes it a hypothesis rather than claiming it.

ideas.what: Sheaf of line bundles with (integrable) connection and the exact sequence relating it to Pic, closed 1-forms mod dlog, and the de Rham Chern class in R^2 f_*(Ω^{≥1})
ideas.modern_name: Pic^♮ / Pic with connection, hypercohomology H^1(X, O^× → Ω^{≥1}), de Rham c_1 in F^1H^2_dR
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: In non-smooth case, obstruction via R^2 f_cris of the augmentation ideal J of the crystalline site
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline first Chern class via log: 1+J ≅ J
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot–Illusie, 'Classes de Chern en cohomologie cristalline' (1970); Mazur–Messing
ideas.where_published: Montréal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1970/74) treat related crystalline Dieudonné theory

ideas.what: Identity component of line bundles with integrable connection = universal vector extension of Pic^0 when Albanese induces iso on 1-forms (curves, abelian torsors)
ideas.modern_name: Pic^♮_0 ≅ E(Pic^0), universal vector extension, H^1_dR = Lie E
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk and Montréal notes discuss universal extensions; exact statement unsure

deep.surprise_reason: Careful working-out of Pic with integrable connection as the universal vector extension, with a crystalline variant for non-smooth X. This matches results published by Messing and Mazur–Messing (who drew on Grothendieck's ideas) around 1973–74. It is a nice record of Grothendieck's own route, but not new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'P^{cri}_{X/S}' should be P^{ci}_{X/S} (integrable connections), consistent with previous and next pages.
'f_*^{dR}' throughout should be f_*^{fl} (pushforward for the fppf site), as defined on the previous page.
'mais si on se place [?] dans le cas où X est lisse sur S' is more likely 'puis, si on précise dans le cas où X est lisse sur S'.
Margin by 'Cas particulier' probably reads 'permis[?] dans 1°)', i.e. a pointer back to section (1); uncertain.
'et en conséquence[?] que c'est l'extension universelle' likely reads 'et on constate que c'est l'extension universelle'.
The insertion '{+de (A,B)+}' is a marginal annotation near the superscript of P, probably 'P^{ci,o}' (identity component).
